guide.pageTitle: Everything you need to know before buying or selling
guide.pageDesc: Documents, taxes, rates and procedures explained clearly. A practical reference so you make decisions with more information and fewer surprises.
guide.disclaimer: Values shown are for reference and may be subject to legal updates. Always consult a professional.
guide.cpcvIntro: The CPCV (Promissory Purchase and Sale Contract) is the contract by which buyer and seller formally commit to signing the final deed. It does not yet transfer ownership, but creates legally binding obligations for both parties. It is typically signed after bank credit approval and before the deed.
guide.cpcvItem1: Full identification of buyer and seller
guide.cpcvItem2: Complete description of the property (address, land registry article, areas)
guide.cpcvItem6: Penalties in case of default by either party
guide.cpcvItem7: Suspensive conditions (e.g. subject to credit approval)
guide.cpcvDepositText: The deposit (sinal) is the amount paid by the buyer as a guarantee. It typically represents 10% to 30% of the sale price, but can be freely agreed between the parties.
guide.cpcvBuyerWithdraws: If the buyer withdraws — they forfeit the entire deposit paid.
guide.cpcvSellerWithdraws: If the seller withdraws — they are obliged to return double the deposit received.
guide.cpcvHighlight: It is strongly recommended that the CPCV be reviewed by a lawyer before signing, especially for high-value transactions.
guide.escrituraIntro: The escritura (deed) is the notarial act that formalises and transfers property ownership. It is signed at a notary or at a Balcão Casa (IRN service) and is mandatory for the transaction to be legally valid and registerable.
guide.escrituraSellerItem1: Updated caderneta predial (land registry card — AT)
guide.escrituraSellerItem2: Certidão do registo predial (land registry certificate — IRNM)
guide.escrituraSellerItem4: Ficha técnica de habitação (for properties post-2004)
guide.escrituraHighlight: IMT and Stamp Duty must be paid before the deed. Bring the payment receipts to the notarial act.
guide.imtIntro: IMT is paid by the buyer before the deed. It is calculated on the higher of the declared purchase price and the property's Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT). Rates vary according to property type and purpose (primary residence, secondary home or other).
guide.imtWarning: For secondary homes or other purposes (rental, commercial), different and generally higher rates apply. Always verify with the Tax Authority or your consultant before completing the acquisition.
guide.imtDisclaimer: Reference values for 2024/2025. Subject to annual government updates. Check the Finance Portal for the exact current values.
guide.isIntro: Stamp Duty applies to acts, contracts and financial operations. In a property transaction it arises at two distinct moments: at the purchase deed and, if there is a mortgage, at the credit agreement.
guide.isDeedDesc: On the higher of the purchase price and the VPT. Paid by the buyer before the deed.
guide.isCreditDesc: On the loan amount granted by the bank. Paid at the time of credit contracting.
guide.imiIntro: IMI is an annual tax collected by the municipality where the property is located. It is levied on the Taxable Patrimonial Value (VPT) determined by the Tax Authority, not on the market price. Each municipality sets its rate annually within a range defined by law.
guide.imiUrbanNote: Rate set annually by the municipality
guide.imiDevolutosNote: Increased coefficient per years of vacancy
guide.imiExemptionText: You may benefit from a temporary IMI exemption for 3 years if the property VPT is equal to or below €125,000 and the household's taxable income does not exceed €153,300. The exemption must be requested from the Tax Authority after acquisition.
guide.imiHighlight: IMI is paid in April (values up to €100), in April and November (€100 to €500), or in three instalments — April, July and November — for values above €500.
guide.creditIntro: The monthly mortgage payment is made up of two parts: the reference rate (index) and the bank's spread. Understanding how each element works is essential to choosing the most suitable financial product for your profile and time horizon.
guide.creditVariableDesc: Indexed to Euribor (3, 6 or 12 months). The payment adjusts periodically with market rate changes. Typically lower in the short term, but exposed to market rises.
guide.creditFixedDesc: The payment remains unchanged for the contracted period (5, 10, 20 years or full term). Offers predictability and protection against market rises, but typically with a higher initial spread.
guide.creditDef1: European interbank rate used as the index for variable-rate mortgages. Changes daily and is published by the ECB.
guide.creditDef2: The bank's margin on top of the index. Reflects the client's credit risk and varies according to LTV and financial profile.
guide.creditDef3: Nominal Annual Rate — sum of the index and spread. The basic rate of the loan.
guide.creditDef4: Annual Percentage Rate — includes TAN, compulsory insurance, commissions and other charges. The true cost of the credit and most relevant for comparing offers.
guide.creditDef5: Ratio of the loan amount to the property value. For primary residence, banks typically finance up to 90%; for secondary homes, up to 80%.
guide.creditDef6: Debt service-to-income ratio — percentage of net monthly income committed to credit payments. The Bank of Portugal recommends a maximum of 35–40%.
guide.creditHighlight: Before contracting, compare the APR not just the spread. Request the FINE (European Standardised Information Sheet) from at least three banks — it is required by law and allows direct comparison between offers.
guide.costsIntro: In addition to the acquisition price, a property transaction involves a set of additional costs that should be budgeted in advance. We present indicative estimates for a primary residence.
guide.costsHighlight: As a practical rule, the buyer should set aside 6% to 10% of the purchase price to cover all transaction, registration and financing costs.
guide.guideCTATitle: I am available to clarify any questions about the process
guide.guideCTABody: Each situation has its specifics. Talk to me to understand exactly what applies to your particular case, with no commitment.
